_comment: Sapient species and the polities they build. The bestiary's opposite number: anything here is a people, and the validator refuses to let a name appear in both files. Provenance works differently from the replicant tree — species and governments have no parents, so the tier letters don't transfer. What's graded instead is whether the books state a thing or leave it open: an acronym is only expanded here if a character expands it on the page.

entries.name: Humans
entries.note: The species the Bobs used to be, and the one they keep having to negotiate with. By book 4 humanity is spread across enough systems that its politics are interstellar rather than national, and the Bobs' relationship to it has drifted from 'us' to something more like a founding generation nobody asked for.

entries.name: Deltans
entries.note: Pre-industrial hunter-gatherers, and the reason the Prime Directive argument runs through the whole series. Bob found them losing a war of attrition to the gorilloids, decided that watching was also a choice, and started handing over better spears. They call him Bawbe. Their word for a family group is hexghi — roughly 'families of our fire' — which is worth knowing because it looks like a species name and isn't.

entries.name: Quinlans
entries.note: The otter-shaped inhabitants of the Heaven's River megastructure, and the most-mentioned people in the books. The Bobs called them Snarks first — Garfield's joke, since they already had Boojums — and Bob insisted the name was provisional until they learned what the Quinlans call themselves. They did. That is the whole ethic of the series in one exchange.

entries.name: Pav
entries.note: Found industrialising hard — Victorian-equivalent, and pumping smoke into their own atmosphere at a rate that made their survival an open question. Jacques named them by elimination: Deltans was taken, Pavonians sounded terrible, so Pav for now. It stuck. They later declined to join the UFS, which the Bobs had gone to the trouble of naming non-human-centrically on the assumption that they would.

entries.name: the Others
entries.note:
Strip-miners of whole systems, and the only species in the books the Bobs fought a war against rather than argued about. Their method was to arrive, consume everything usable including the inhabitants, and move on — which is what turns the Bobs from explorers into a defence force. The name is a placeholder that stopped being one.

Bill puts a composite scan image of one in front of the moot in Bk2 ch57, and it is the most detailed physical description of any species in the books. About four feet, never standing straight, shading from an oily green-violet sheen through grey to black. He tells the room to start from a gorilla's posture — not quite on four limbs, not quite upright — with front limbs like meaty wings ending in thick suckered digits for gripping prey rather than handling tools, and a back end he compares to a sea lion's with a tail added to a split one. The front opens in a vertical slash into a maw that grinds and strips rather than chews, with dexterous feeding fingers folding out of it. The head carries the senses and a ring of small eyes around its dome for vision in every direction, while what appears to be the brain sits high on the trunk instead. The scans also showed them packed at the density of a crowded room throughout the living space, which is what settles the hive reading.

entries.name: FAITH
entries.cite: Bk1 ch4 · Bob, July 15, 2133; Bk2 · List of Terms
entries.note:
The theocracy that owned Bob's frozen head, and the state whose information policy denied him his own family records — under FAITH, nothing is public by default. No character ever unpacks the acronym, and this register recorded that gap for as long as it was true. The List of Terms at the back of book 2 expands it, which is Taylor rather than a character but is still printed in the novel. Recorded now with that distinction rather than the gap.

@bk5 Not defunct, which this register had it as. FAITH outlives the state and the planet both: Romulus was settled mostly by FAITH citizens, and several generations later it is running slates there, doing better than expected, and finally taking a majority government. Will names its resurgence and the rise of the Luddies as two wars in the making. A theocracy that lost its world and came back as a party is a different thing from one that ended.

entries.name: USE
entries.note: One of the powers of Bob's second lifetime, and expanded on the page by Dr. Landers. Bob's opinion was that the name was grandiose given how little of Eurasia it covered; Landers pointed out that the old USA hadn't covered all of America either.

entries.name: Brazilian Empire
entries.note: A rival power of the same era, and one of the states whose competing colony ships turned the launch window into a shooting match. Sparsely mentioned but consequential: the war it takes part in is what leaves Earth uninhabitable.

entries.name: VEHEMENT
entries.expansion: Voluntary Extinction of Human Existence Means Earth's Natural Transformation
entries.note: Anti-human extremists who held that humanity had had its chance and should be allowed to die out — and who were prepared to help. Colonel Butterworth supplies the expansion and immediately undercuts it: that, or something close to it, he had heard several variants and one or two obscene ones. The expansion is recorded here with that hedge intact, because the hedge is the citation.

entries.name: the Spits
entries.note: A survivor enclave on Spitsbergen, led by Gudmund Valter, and one of the groups Riker had to ration a dying planet between. Their island was likely to become uninhabitable first, which gave every conversation with them a deadline. Easy to mistake for a species from the word alone; it is a place with people on it.

entries.name: UFS
entries.note: The interstellar federation of the later books, whose name the Bobs deliberately kept free of anything human-centric so that other species could join without feeling annexed. The Pav declined anyway. Will's summary of the resulting council sessions is not printable in a family register.

entries.name: Pangean Council
entries.note: The colonial government that formally went to war with a faction of the Bobiverse. Its statement is careful to describe Starfleet as devices rather than people, and to call the name disparaging — a government drawing the personhood line exactly where it finds convenient, which is the same line the Bobs spend five books arguing about from the other side.

entries.name: the Administrator
entries.note: The governing power inside Heaven's River, enforcing a set of rules called the Limits. Quinlans discuss it the way people discuss weather that can evict them — fairness is explicitly not part of its vocabulary, and it cannot be stopped, only avoided. Whether it counts as a government, a maintenance system or a person is left open.

entries.name: Quinlan Resistance
entries.note: Quinlans organised against the Administrator and the Limits. They matter to the argument the books are making: a people the Bobs first labelled Snarks turn out to have their own politics, their own factions and their own dissidents, none of which needed outside help to exist.

entries.name: Dragons
entries.note:
Jabberwocky's intelligent species, and the Bobs' name for them rather than their own — Mario named them on discovering the planet, and Howard's reaction was that they look more like squirrels. They live in three-dimensional medieval and Renaissance villages built on the backs of floaters, fish for trout on the wing, keep written records, and are conquered during the books by a dragon called Alexander whose army the Bobs call the Alexandrians.

Bridget's survey found they have no general word for themselves at all: they identify by village, and regard the residents of other villages as barely above talking animals. That is the personhood argument the whole series runs on, appearing for once inside a species rather than between two.

Howard and Bridget walk among them in dragon mannies without telling them, which is `covert` in the same sense as the Quinlans.

entries.name: Roanokians
entries.note:
About human height, bipedal and broadly humanoid, with disproportionately long arms and large hands — Dae's guess is an ambush predator ancestry. Icarus and Dae name them for the world they name Roanoke, after the colony that vanished leaving a word carved on a post, and name their own ship Croatoan after the word. The name is the Bobs': the species' own is known, but only in writing, because the library was scanned before the audio was.

They are gone and it was deliberate — no bodies, no abandoned vehicles, no sign of haste, the ecology untouched, the libraries still maintained. The Archivist's account is that they stored their entire population, body and mind, and transmitted them to ships already centuries under way. Whether anyone in that transmission is awake is a question it will not answer, which is why this entry's standing is unknown rather than extinct.

entries.name: Poseidon Administrative Council
entries.note: The colonial government of Poseidon, and the one this register can watch being overthrown. Marcus works for it without holding any position it could not drop him from, then helps run the revolution against it; five of its seven councillors are captured and two are thought to have left by submarine. What replaced it is deliberately weak — a generation later, Poseidon citizenry are described as having no tolerance for a central authority, given their history.

entries.name: Newholme Council
entries.note: The colonial government of Newholme, known locally as the Big Heads, which issued a military arrest order for Claude by executive order and later put facial recognition into everything on the reasonable theory that it would make life hard for Bobs. Its citizens responded by all wearing masks of the president, Adrianne Hernandez, and committing public mischief in her face for a week. The policy did not change.

entries.name: New Jerusalem
entries.note: The FAITH colony's own polity, run by Cranston, who is Minister and then President and who tried to prohibit Howard's alcohol on a world where the Spits were already supplying it. It became a full democracy after incriminating video got out and he stood down, at which point the citizenry separated church and state again — a decision that did not stick, since FAITH is winning elections there two books later.

entries.name: the Luddies
entries.note: The anti-manny, anti-replicant activist movement of the later books — Bridget's phrase for them. Their platform is the unfairness of what replicants can do, and by book 5 they are winning the employment argument against ex-humans on many UFS worlds, to the point where a professor can no longer teach. Will names them alongside a resurgent FAITH as one of two wars in the making.

entries.name: Ever Onward Society
entries.note: Fifteen thousand Romulans who signed up to leave rather than live under the politics at home, and the vehicle Will had been quietly building for the same purpose — he and Herschel found they had been designing the same escape independently. Herschel's own estimate is that a lot of the membership were playing at it or voting with their names, which is what makes the number worth recording rather than believing.

entries.name: Pan Galactic Federation
entries.note: An interstellar power the Bobs meet only through its infrastructure: an automated station warning Icarus and Dae out of an interdicted antimatter works, then handing over its own communication protocols when asked. The name is a translation out of Roanokian and Icarus says so at the time — how accurate it is, is exactly the question he raises and never gets to answer. Its scouts had reached the Bobs' neighbourhood at some point; the wreckage on Jabberwocky carries a Federation serial number.

entries.name: Zjentfen
entries.note: The Pav country Jacques learned first, by parking drones in the shadows of reading clubs and scanning whatever was read aloud — a month's work for a working vocabulary. Its people called themselves Zjentfen and their language Tinozj. Named once, and then the Others stripped the planet. It is here because a nation that gets one sentence and no second one is still a nation, and the register's job is to say so rather than round it off.

entries.name: China
entries.note: One of the six powers Bob is briefed on, holding about 80% of Earth between them, and loosely aligned with the Brazilian Empire against the USE and FAITH. It sabotaged the USE facility before launch and was retaliated against, which is part of how the launch window turned into a shooting match.

entries.name: the Australian Federation
entries.note: One of the six powers, and the one with a consequence the others do not have: it was working on the probe concept independently, FAITH stole its insights, and it launched anyway. Its replicant is Henry Roberts, whom Linus finds at Epsilon Indi — an entire second line of replicants from a programme that officially did not exist. Brazil dropped rocks on Australia; the survivors ended up in New Zealand.

entries.name: the Republic of Africa
entries.note: One of the six powers, and the one Bob stops to be rude about: he calls the name a laughable irony given how little of Africa it covers, which is the same joke he makes about the United States of Eurasia a paragraph earlier. It and Australia spend the pre-launch crisis warning everyone not to involve them.

entries.name: Starfleet
entries.note: The loudest of the four, and the only one that fought a war. It stripped its own genealogy and location records out of the databases, which is why two records in this register are tier X: for a Starfleet Bob the missing lineage is not a gap in anyone's reading, it is the deletion itself. A colonial government went to war with it and was careful, in its own prepared statement, to call its members devices rather than people.

entries.name: the Skippies
entries.note: Bobs who went for raw intelligence, dropped names for numeric designations and speech for packetized communication, and still answer to nicknames when dealing with anyone else. They built the super AI, and Skippyland was still under quarantine a decade later. Their representative on the Heaven's River expedition wears a grey coverall and is called Hugh.

entries.name: the Gamers
entries.note: Bobs who play, at length and in character, and who turn out to be the ones you want when a megastructure airlock has to be opened without tripping anything. Their leader is Gandalf; the campaign is real enough that Kevin died in it and was resurrected for a fee payable in everything he had left.

entries.name: the Borg
entries.note: Bobs who merged their processing rather than staying separate people, and the faction whose name is the bluntest joke in the Bobiverse about what the others are afraid of. Their representative on the Heaven's River expedition wanted the handle Hugh and had to settle for Locutus, in a getup with rather more armour than the television original.
